summary: Henry Harkness was an Indologist and linguist. He served as secretary at the College of Fort St. George until 1834, and later as secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland from 1834 to 1837.

Henry Hart Milman worked in Indology and history/archaeology. Educated at Eton and Brasenose College, Oxford, under adviser Horace Hayman Wilson, he served as Professor of Poetry at the University of Oxford from 1821 to 1831.

Henry Heras studied at Col·legi del Sagrat Cor and worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He taught at Colegio del Salvador, became a professor at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, in 1923, and founded the Heras Institute in 1926.

Henry Herbert Dodwell, a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology, studied at Lord Williams's School and St John's College, Oxford. He served in the Indian Education Service (1908–1922) and was a professor of history at SOAS (1922–1946).

Henry Hoenigswald studied linguistics and Indology at Munich, Zurich, Padua, and Florence under Giacomo Devoto. He held posts at Yale, Hartford Seminary, and the University of Pennsylvania, where he was Associate Professor of Linguistics from 1948 to 1985.

Henry Hughes Presler worked in religious studies and Indology after earning degrees from North Dakota State, Boston University, and the University of Chicago. He was a missionary with the United Methodist Board (1937–1972) and taught at Leonard Theological College.

Educated at Pembroke College, Cambridge, Henry James Sumner Maine worked in history/archaeology and Indology. He held professorships at Cambridge and Oxford, served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Calcutta (~1862–1869), and was Master of Trinity Hall (1877–1888).

Henry Lee Shuttleworth, a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology, studied at Pembroke College, Oxford, and the University of Cambridge. He served as an Additional Lecturer and later Lecturer in Tibetan at SOAS University of London (1936–1948).
Henry Martyn was a scholar in linguistics and religious studies. He was educated at Truro Cathedral School and St John's College, and he studied under John Borthwick Gilchrist around 1804–1805.
Henry Miers Elliot was an Indologist and historian who studied at Winchester College from around 1820 to 1826. He served as a civil servant for the East India Company from approximately 1827 to 1853.
Henry Morris, an Indologist and historian, studied at Rugby School and the East India Company College. He served in the Madras Civil Service from 1848 to 1875, holding the post of Judge of Godavery.

Henry Nelson Wright was an Indologist and historian who studied classics at Corpus Christi College, Oxford. He served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1892 to 1924 and founded the Numismatic Society of India in 1910.

Henry Octavius Coxe studied at Westminster School and Worcester College before working in history and archaeology. He held a post at the British Museum (1833–1838) and served as Librarian at the Bodleian Library from 1839 to 1881.
Henry Pitts Forster was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He joined the East India Company's Bengal Civil Service in 1783 and later served as Master of the Calcutta Mint from 1803 to 1804.

Henry R. Hoisington, an Indologist and religious studies scholar, studied at Williams College and Auburn Theological Seminary. He served as a missionary with the American Ceylon Mission and as principal of Batticotta Seminary from approximately 1835 to 1849.

Henry Rawlinson was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history/archaeology, and linguistics. He served as Director of the Royal Asiatic Society in 1862 and later as its President from 1878 to 1881.
Henry Rice was an Indologist who served as a missionary for the London Missionary Society from around 1869 to 1880, and subsequently for the Church of Scotland from 1880 to 1905.

Henry Snyder Gehman studied at Franklin & Marshall, UPenn, Dropsie College, and EDS. An Indologist, linguist, and religious studies scholar, he taught Semitic languages at Princeton University and was Professor of O.T. at Princeton Theological Seminary (1930–1958).
Henry Steel Olcott worked in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at Columbia University from around 1847 to 1849 and founded the Theosophical Society in 1875.

Henry Sullivan Jarrett, a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology, studied at Prior Park College. He served as Secretary and Member of the Board of Examiners at Fort William (1870–1894) and Assistant Secretary in the Legislative Department.
